newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- off slightly after data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- off slightly after data.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds were off slightly in early Wednesday trading, as market participants awaited a massive taxable deal and more economic data.
New Jersey's Economic Development Authority plans to sell $2.75 billion of taxable bonds through Merrill Lynch & Co, but traders said the tax-exempt market is not taking much notice.
"It really doesn't impact our market because it's taxable," one trader said.
The Commerce Department reported that May durable goods orders fell 0.6 percent, compared to an upwardly revised 1.8 percent for the month. Economists had expected a 0.6-percent rise.
Analysts said the figure reinforces perceptions that the Federal Reserve will hold interest rates steady at its July policy meeting.
Treasury bonds recovered somewhat from deeper losses after the data. The benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury bond lost 9/32 at 98-27/32 to yield 6.72 percent.
In debt futures, the September municipal contract was off 4/32 at 117-8/32. The September T-bond contract was off 7/32 at 111-30/32.
Existing home sales for May are set for release at 1000 EDT, and economists are expecting the figure to be 4.07 million.
Municipal bond sales for Wednesday are expected to total $4 billion in 35 deals, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Negotiated offerings total $3.6 billion in 20 sales, with the New Jersey deal topping the list.
On the competitive side, 15 sales totaling $325 million are scheduled. A $69 million New York Environmental deal at 1100 EDT is the largest.
